content.user_title: Improve App Store Listings with ASO Fundamentals
content.value_statement: Unclear metadata and weak keyword choices can make app store listings harder to discover and understand. This skill guides listing copy, keyword placement, and conversion priorities without requiring live analytics or an API key.
actual_capabilities: Explain how Apple and Google differ in keyword indexing and searchable metadata.
Review supplied titles, subtitles, descriptions, and Apple keyword fields against the documented guidance.
Organize candidate keywords into primary, secondary, long-tail, and aspirational tiers.
Suggest benefit-focused listing copy and screenshot sequencing.
Recommend rating prompt timing and explain the role of review replies.
Prioritize listing improvements and outline market-specific localization considerations.
limitations: Does not retrieve live ranks, search volumes, keyword difficulty, competitor metrics, or app scores.
Provides written guidance only; it does not publish listings, create visual assets, or run store experiments.
Store policies and limits can change; release-critical details require confirmation against current official documentation.
Cannot guarantee rankings, installs, conversion improvements, or marketplace approval.

use_cases.title: Prepare a first app listing
use_cases.description: Draft a title, subtitle, and keyword plan for a new app using its audience and main benefits.

use_cases.title: Review listing copy across stores
use_cases.description: Compare supplied Apple and Google listings, identify keyword placement problems, and prioritize copy improvements.

use_cases.title: Plan a localized listing
use_cases.description: Build a market-specific metadata research checklist and align screenshot messages with a new audience.

prompt_templates.title: Understand ASO basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain ASO for my [app type]. Compare Apple and Google keyword indexing, then give me five listing improvements to consider.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: learn the main concepts without analytics.

prompt_templates.title: Review supplied metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this [Apple or Google] listing: [paste metadata]. Flag repeated keywords, unclear benefits, and field-limit issues. Suggest revised copy without inventing performance data.

prompt_templates.title: Build a keyword placement plan
prompt_templates.prompt: My app serves [audience] and provides [benefits]. Candidate keywords: [terms]. Group them into four tiers and suggest placements for [store]. Mark demand and competition as unverified.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: structure keyword hypotheses before collecting live data.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a localized ASO iteration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these listings, audience notes, and screenshot descriptions: [materials]. Plan improvements for [markets] across metadata, screenshots, rating prompts, and localization. Define one-change experiments and identify missing evidence. Do not promise rankings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a broader listing optimization plan.

output_examples.input: For a hypothetical habit app named Lumen, suggest an Apple title and subtitle without ranking claims.
output: The title states the app category, while the subtitle adds a benefit and distinct terms.
These are copy suggestions, not evidence of keyword demand or ranking potential.

output_examples.input: My Google Play description is a repeated keyword list, and my first screenshot only shows a logo. What should I improve first?
output: Replace repeated keyword blocks with natural sentences describing the app audience, benefits, and main tasks.
Review the title and short description for clear positioning and relevant terms.
Use the first screenshot to show the app performing its strongest task, with a concise benefit caption.
Test one listing change at a time and use your own store analytics to evaluate results.

best_practices: Provide the target store, audience, locale, and current metadata before requesting specific recommendations.
Confirm release-critical rules and field limits against current Apple or Google documentation.
Treat keyword suggestions as hypotheses and validate them with real market data before prioritizing experiments.
anti_patterns: Requesting precise ranks, search volumes, or competitor scores without supplying data or connecting separate analytics tools.
Stuffing keywords, using competitor trademarks, or fabricating reviews and unsupported performance claims.
Translating keywords literally across markets or changing every listing element before measuring results.

faq.question: Do I need an ASOScan API key?
faq.answer: No. This skill provides general ASO guidance without an API key or live analytics.

faq.question: Which app stores does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Apple App Store and Google Play metadata, keyword placement, visual asset strategy, ratings, and localization.

faq.question: Can it report my actual app rankings?
faq.answer: No. Actual rankings and keyword metrics require supplied evidence or separate data skills with connected ASOScan tools or an API key.

faq.question: Can it improve listing text I provide?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review supplied metadata and suggest clearer titles, subtitles, descriptions, and keyword placement based on its guidance.

faq.question: Does it publish updates or generate screenshots?
faq.answer: No. It offers copy and visual strategy recommendations, but includes no publishing workflow or screenshot generation tools.

faq.question: Are its recommendations guaranteed to be current or improve rankings?
faq.answer: No. Store rules change, and rankings depend on multiple factors. Verify critical policies and measure changes using your own analytics.
